newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian airport sales process to quicken.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian airport sales process to quicken.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday it was likely to conclude the first phase of its A$2.0 billion airport privatisation plan ahead of schedule.
"The process is going well and it may well be that we can accelerate the selling process a little quicker than was previously indicated," a spokesman for Finance Minister John Fahey told Reuters.

However, the spokesman declined to nominate a specific date for the completion of the sale process, saying only that it could be a "few weeks" ahead of schedule. The sale process was originally expected to be finalised by June 30 next year.
The government has received 26 expressions of interest for Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth airports, which are up for sale as the first phase of the privatisation plan.
The spokesman said January 30 remained the deadline for formal bids for the three airports. It was the next stage of the process that would take less time than previously anticipated, he said.
The government will treat the January 30 bids as final bids, thus erasing the possibility of bidders claiming the tenders were only indicative and thus allowing them to make changes at a later date.

The Australian government won parliamentary approval for the sale of the country's main airports in September and almost immediately advertised throughout the country for bidders for 50-year leases for the first round of airports.
Adelaide airport may also be sold in the 1996/97 year with the remaining airports scheduled to be sold in 1997/98.
Sydney airport and the city's planned second airport are the only possible exceptions with their sales being delayed as a result of noise and environment studies.

Fahey's spokesman said he couldn't comment on whether the sale of the other airports would be brought forward as a result of the quickening of the sale process for Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth airports.
"That's still to be determined," he said.
